text: A situation involving either (i) the resort to armed force between two or more States, regardless of intensity or duration (known as an International Armed Conflict), or (ii) armed violence between a State and one or more organized non-State armed groups, or between such groups, where the violence reaches a sufficient level of intensity and the non-State armed forces possess a sufficient degree of organization (non-international Armed Conflict).

A machine-based system that, for explicit or implicit objectives, infers, from the input it receives, how to generate outputs such as predictions, content, recommendations, or decisions that can influence physical or virtual environments. Different AI systems vary in their levels of autonomy and adaptiveness after deployment.
Every human being below the age of eighteen years unless under the law applicable to the Child, majority is attained earlier.

All objects that are not Military Objectives. International Humanitarian Law prohibits acts of violence, attacks, and reprisals against Civilian Objects. For the purpose of this Agreement, Civilian Objects include internet and communications infrastructure, such as routers, undersea cables, Internet Service Providers (ISPs), and Data centers – including those used for civilian communications, finance, education, healthcare, and elections. Civilian Objects remain civilian insofar as they do not, by their nature, location, purpose, or use, make an effective contribution to military action and their total or partial destruction, capture, or neutralization, in the circumstances ruling at the time, offers a definite military advantage.
A team that performs, coordinates, and supports the response to security incidents involving sites within a defined constituency.

Actions or mechanisms undertaken by Parties to enhance trust, transparency, and predictability. CBMs can promote stability and help to reduce the risk of misunderstanding and conflict. Examples of CBMs may include establishment of points of contact between cyber incident response teams, notification of high-risk cyber activities, or voluntary reporting of potential breaches.
A structured group of three or more persons that exists over a period of time and acts together to commit serious crimes for the purpose of obtaining a financial or other material benefit.

Cyber Attack is a Cyber Operation that may be reasonably expected to result in the damage or destruction of objects or the injury or death of people. Such operations do not need to have a direct impact on objects or people and can be considered an attack even if the impact is indirect, provided there is a reasonably foreseeable causal link between the operation and the harm caused. For the purposes of this Agreement, a Cyber Attack may include disabling the functionality of the target itself, even if no physical damage is caused. A Cyber Operation aimed at obtaining unauthorized access to information does not, in itself, constitute a Cyber Attack. However, such an operation may constitute a Cyber Attack where it can reasonably be expected to cause, directly or indirectly, injury or death to persons or damage, disabling, or destruction of objects. For the purposes of this Agreement, an attack on Data that results in destruction or death also qualifies as a Cyber Attack.^,^
A Cyber Operation refers to any act conducted through or against a computer network or system, including software, hardware, and Data, that is intended to achieve objectives in or through Cyberspace.

The global, interconnected domain made up of Digital networks, Information and Communication Technologies, and the Data that flows through them, including the infrastructure and systems that enable Digital communication, storage, and computation.

Companies or individuals that develop, sell, and/or facilitate offensive cyber capabilities which enable a Party to access the networks, computers, phones, or internet-connected devices of another Party.
Information stored, processed, or transmitted in Digital form, typically using computers or networks, and may include files, databases, communications, metadata, software, and system configurations.

A malicious attempt to flood a targeted adversary’s network, system, or service with excessive incoming traffic or requests from many different sources to overload and potentially take the network offline, making it unavailable for its intended users. A Distributed Denial of Service Attack (DDoS) is a Denial of Service Attack that uses multiple computers or machines to flood a targeted source.

Synthetic, AI-manipulated, or AI-generated audio, visual, or audiovisual content that has the effect of deceiving the audience into believing that fabricated or altered voices, images, videos, or events are authentic, thereby misleading the audience into thinking that something occurred when it did not or did not occur when it did.
Digital Operations, which can be carried out in Armed Conflict, Grey Zone Activity, and Internal Disturbance, that the Parties agree to De-escalate for the purposes of this Agreement.

The reduction in the intensity, frequency, scope, and/or harmful effects of Digital Operations, with the aim of reducing tensions, preventing further escalation, limiting harm, or creating conditions for dialogue, stability, or peace. De-escalation may occur in the context of Grey Zone Activity or Internal Disturbance and does not require the complete cessation of Digital Operations. De-escalation may also occur in the context of Armed Conflict, although the term ceasefire is traditionally understood to mean the suspension or cessation of hostilities in the context of an Armed Conflict.

Electronic systems, devices, or processes that rely on computing technology, software, and Data networks for communication, automation, artificial intelligence, and/or interaction. This can include hardware, software, Data, and Digital services, as well as activities carried out in or through Cyberspace. Digital encompasses all forms of information that are stored, transmitted, processed, or manipulated in binary form (i.e., using 0s and 1s).

Any activity conducted through, against, or using Digital technologies, Information and Communications Technologies, computer systems or networks, social media and communications platforms, or Data, for the purpose of producing effects in the Digital or physical environment. Digital Operations include, but are not limited to, Cyber Operations, information operations conducted through Digital means, interference with communications or internet services, and the creation, manipulation, dissemination, or amplification of Digital content.

Hardware, software, networks, and Data systems that enable Digital Operations and Digital communications. This includes physical components, such as servers, cables, routers, and satellites, as well as logical and functional components, such as software, social media and communications platforms, and protocols enabling services and Data exchange.
When Parties are not engaged in Prohibited Digital Operations with other Parties to this Agreement.
The monitoring of Digital communications and activities of individuals or groups using technology such as computer software, Internet monitoring tools, and Data analytics.

Deliberately false, misleading, or inaccurate information that has the effect of deceiving and results in serious reputational, financial, legal, psychological, or physical injury to persons or the damage or destruction of Civilian Objects or Military Objectives. This includes information that influences public opinion or obscures the truth. Irony, satire, parody, or humour that seeks to question or ridicule are not forms of Disinformation.^,^
The act of exposing private or identifying information on the internet about an individual or group without the individual’s or group’s consent, usually with malicious intent.

Objects, facilities, Data, or infrastructure, that can be used for both civilian and military purposes. Dual-Use technologies can be used by civilians for peaceful means while also being adaptable for or supplementary to warfare, intelligence, or weapons development. The Dual-Use framework in this definition applies in the context of Armed Conflict. In Grey Zone Activity and Internal Disturbance, the characterization of objects and their protection is governed by applicable International Law, including International Human Rights Law, rather than the International Humanitarian Law Dual-Use framework

A form of electronic warfare in which an actor deliberately emits radio-frequency or other electromagnetic energy to overwhelm, confuse, or block the reception of signals used for communication, navigation, sensing, or control.

The space in which State or non-State actors engage in coercive, hostile, or destabilizing activities that generally remain below the threshold of a "use of force" under Article 2(4) of the UN Charter and an “armed attack” under Article 51. Grey Zone activities do not, by themselves, amount to Armed Conflict under International Humanitarian Law. Grey Zone is not a legal term, nor a term used in International Law.
Obtaining unauthorized access to or manipulating Data, systems, networks, or devices, including through the exploitation of vulnerabilities.
For the purpose of this Agreement, a retaliatory Cyber Operation undertaken against the actual or suspected source of a Cyber Attack.

Any kind of communication in speech, writing, or behavior, that attacks or uses pejorative or discriminatory language with reference to a person or a group on the basis of who they are, based on their religion, ethnicity, nationality, race, color, descent, gender, age, sexual orientation, disability, political affiliation, or other identity factor. The internet and social media and communications platforms can be used to spread Hate Speech.
Companies that develop, operate, or provide Digital technologies and infrastructure used to capture, transmit, or display electronic Data or information.

The creation, use, or dissemination of information that is false, misleading, manipulated, or otherwise weaponized in a manner that is intended, or reasonably likely, to cause significant physical, psychological, economic, or social harm to individuals and/or communities or materially undermine societal trust, humanitarian operations, civic institutions, democratic processes, or peace processes through deceptive, manipulative, or otherwise harmful information practices. In this Handbook, Information Threats include Misinformation and Disinformation, Manipulated Media, Inauthentic Behavior, Doxxing, Online Incitement to Violence, Hate Speech, Online Recruitment, Malicious Online Advertisements, Interference with Humanitarian Information and Data, Harassment of Journalists and Media, and Intimidating Diaspora.

Deliberate disruptions or restriction of access to internet services or Digital communications. In this Handbook, Internet Interference includes Internet Shutdowns, Throttling, Attacks on Internet Infrastructure, Electronic Jamming, and Third-Party Internet Interference.

Situations of serious internal disorder involving acts of violence, such as riots or isolated or sporadic acts of violence, which do not amount to an Armed Conflict. International Humanitarian Law does not apply here but other forms of International Law, including International Human Rights Law, remain applicable.

An intentional disruption of internet or electronic communications, rendering the internet or electronic communications inaccessible or effectively unusable, for a specific population or within a specific location, often to exert control over the flow of information.

Physical or virtual acts directed against the technical infrastructure that enables the functioning, routing, or transmission of the internet or other Digital communications, including radio transmission towers, fiber-optic and undersea cables, satellites, internet exchange points, routing systems, and associated hardware or software, that are intended or reasonably expected to disrupt, degrade, disable, or manipulate connectivity or communication flows.

Paid or sponsored Digital content distributed through social media and communications platforms to promote messages, influence perceptions, or shape behavior. Malicious Online Advertisements may be used to distribute or amplify harmful information.

Any software or code intentionally designed to or reasonably expected to disrupt, damage, degrade, or gain unauthorized access to a computer system, device, server Data, or network. Malware includes, but is not limited to, viruses, worms, Trojan horses, ransomware, Spyware, adware, and other forms of malicious code.

An object is considered a Military Objective under International Humanitarian Law if, by its nature, location, purpose, or use, it makes an effective contribution to military action, and its total or partial destruction, capture, or neutralization offers a definite military advantage. For further clarification, see the definitions of Civilian Object and Dual-Use.
Verifiably false, inaccurate, or misleading information that is shared, disseminated, or amplified without the intention to deceive, manipulate, or cause harm.

Any Digital communication, including on but not limited to social media and communications platforms, websites, videos, and forums that is intended to, and reasonably likely to, incite discrimination, hostility, or violence against individuals or groups of people. Online speech is assessed using the Rabat Plan of Action six-part threshold test (context, speaker, intent, content, extent, likelihood of harm) to determine whether it qualifies as incitement to violence.
The use of social media and communications platforms by Parties to enlist, recruit, or solicit individuals for participation in the Armed Conflict, Grey Zone Activity, or Internal Disturbance.

A form of Cyber Operation whereby the attacker uses deceptive communications, often emails, websites, or messages, to trick individuals to disclose confidential information, provide access to credentials, or install Malicious Software.
Digital Operations, which can be carried out in Armed Conflict, Grey Zone Activity, and Internal Disturbance, that the Parties agree to cease for the purposes of this Agreement.

Third Party State, non-State, or quasi-State groups or individuals that are supported – politically, financially, and/or militarily – by a Party to advance their strategic objectives, often allowing the Proxy Actor to influence the conflict without becoming a Party. The conduct of Proxy Actors may be attributable to a State in accordance with applicable rules of International Law.

Critical, foundational infrastructure that enables the global internet to function reliably and securely, including packet routing and forwarding, naming and numbering systems, cryptographic mechanisms of security and identity, and physical transmission media.

The falsification or impersonation of a digital identity, source, address, communication, or other identifying information to deceive a person or digital system into believing that the information or communication originates from a legitimate or different source.

Malicious Software designed to covertly access or compromise a person’s or institution’s device in order to monitor, collect, or intercept Data, communications, or metadata relating to that person, institution, or their networks, without their knowledge or consent.

Monitoring, collection, interception, retention, or analysis of Data or communications relating to a person, group, or system, by Digital or electronic means, whether targeted or indiscriminate, for purposes of intelligence gathering, security, control, influence, or operational advantage.

Any act, that is committed, assisted, aggravated, or amplified by the use of ICTs or other digital tools, that results in or is likely to result in physical, sexual, psychological, social, political or economic harm, or other infringements of rights and freedoms.
The use or threatened use of violence, or other acts dangerous to human life, intended to intimidate or coerce a civilian population or to influence government policy or conduct.
An organization that engages in, or has the capability and intent to engage in, such terrorist activity.

Any State, organization, company, Proxy Actor, or other entity that is not a principal Party to the Armed Conflict, Grey Zone Activity, or Internal Disturbance but intervenes, sometimes indirectly, to influence its outcome by supporting, assisting, participating in, enabling, or otherwise becoming involved with a Party. Third Parties can provide resources like arms, funding, training, personnel, or other Digital capabilities.
Intentional technical measures used to reduce the speed, capacity, or reliability of Digital communications networks or services, thereby impairing users’ ability to access or transmit information.
